subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit, daily, and idle resets, and what blocking, background, config, and security rules should govern it?
rationale: Current code can mechanically expose reset hooks, but choosing a silent reset-time agent execution path affects user consent, security boundaries, provider/auth routing, plugin ownership, and reset latency.

options.title: Approve bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Implement a single reset-memory policy with explicit timeout, dedupe, audit/redaction, sandbox, provider/auth, and opt-out or consent rules across manual, daily, and idle resets.

options.title: Keep reset hooks mechanical
options.body: Limit reset persistence to lifecycle hooks and startup context, and route agentic curation to explicit user commands or compaction only.

options.title: Defer to plugin API design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a plugin-contract design item until reset lifecycle events can safely request curation without core-owned silent agent execution.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Implement a single reset-memory policy with explicit timeout, dedupe, audit/redaction, sandbox, provider/auth, and opt-out or consent rules across manual, daily, and idle resets.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested behavior extends the pre-compaction memory-flush feature and reset command policy that steipete introduced or shaped.
